featured_reviews.name: Dharmesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
They have Jain food available, which is a plus, but the service and overall experience leave much to be desired. The space is very small, with only 2-3 tables to serve, making it feel cramped. If you ask for water, you’ll get only one glass as they don’t have a jug facility, and if you need a second glass, you’ll have to wait. The food is great, though slightly overpriced. They provide a finger bowl with cold water, but if you ask for warm water, they simply deny it. I requested extra mouth freshener at the end, and the staff looked at us as if we had committed a crime, sternly stating that they only provide two mouth fresheners. The restaurant comes across as stingy in every aspect, whether it’s water or something as small as a mouth freshener. While the Jain food is good, the service and ambiance definitely need improvement.

Edit and reply :

I must say it left a lasting impression on me regarding their service ethics. While the customer shared their experience about limited service and feeling unwelcome when requesting simple extras like a mouth freshener or warm water, the response from the restaurant seemed to justify these shortcomings rather than addressing them empathetically.

Highlighting that the guest asked for extra gravy or carried their own water bottle seems unnecessary and detracts from the core concern of providing a welcoming experience. Great hospitality is about going the extra mile, especially for small gestures that enhance customer satisfaction. Defending such practices as part of policy might reflect on the work ethic and priorities of the establishment.

Good food is important, but customer care and a positive dining experience matter just as much, if not more. I hope the restaurant considers this feedback seriously and strives for improvement.

featured_reviews.name: Vinit Vinayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Muthuswamy Cafe, and it was an amazing experience for anyone who loves authentic South Indian food.

The place has a simple yet comforting vibe, and the aroma itself sets the mood as soon as you walk in. The food is absolutely top-notch—fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. From crispy dosas to soft idlis and rich sambhar, everything tasted authentic and satisfying.

The service was quick and efficient, and the staff was polite and attentive throughout. It’s one of those places where you go for the food and end up loving the whole experience.

If you’re in Dadar and craving real South Indian flavors, this spot is definitely worth visiting!

featured_reviews.name: Himanshi Patel
featured_reviews.review_text: Café Muthuswami in Dadar is a cozy spot that brings authentic South Indian flavors to life. Known for its crispy dosas, soft idlis, and rich, aromatic filter coffee, every bite feels comforting and nostalgic. The ambiance is simple yet inviting, perfect for casual catch-ups or a relaxed solo meal. Service is quick, and the food quality is consistently impressive. Whether you’re craving a hearty breakfast or a light evening snack, this café delivers on both taste and experience. A must-visit for anyone who loves traditional South Indian food in Mumbai with a homely touch and great value.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Fulsundar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mutuswami Cafe is located just outside Dadar East railway station, so it’s very easy to find and perfect for a quick stop after travel. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, which is nice if you want to sit comfortably or just grab something quickly.
We tried the strawberry milkshake & mango milkshake both were thick, chilled, and refreshing. The paper masala dosa was big, crispy, and came with good chutney and sambar. Kanchipuram idli was soft and flavourful, a little different from regular idli and worth trying.
Cheese tava rice was spicy, cheesy, and filling good if you’re very hungry. We ended with pineapple sheera, which was warm, slightly sweet, and had a nice fruity taste.
Overall, it’s a good place for South Indian food and quick snacks near the station.

featured_reviews.name: VISHAL UPADHYAY
featured_reviews.review_text: We ordered cheese pav bhaji, and masala dosa and both were extremely delicious. We loved both the items. Cost wise it appeared a little costly given the ambience, and quality of service. It was situated near Dadar railway station and is fine for some snacking.

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re in Dadar and craving authentic South Indian flavors any time of the day, Muttuswami Cafe is the place to be!
This is the only café in the area open 24/7, making it a perfect spot for early breakfasts, late-night cravings, or casual meetups at any hour.
The food quality is outstanding, with every dish served fresh, flavorful, and satisfying:
Cheese Pav Bhaji – perfectly buttery with a generous layer of melted cheese that elevates the classic taste.
Podi Idli – soft, bite-sized idlis coated beautifully in spicy podi masala and ghee.
Muttuswami Special Benne Dosa – rich, crispy, and soaked in butter with a delicious traditional touch.
Spring Dosa – a unique fusion twist, crispy outside with a flavorful stuffed filling inside.
Fruit Custard Dessert – creamy, refreshing, and loaded with fresh fruits for the perfect sweet ending.
Their fresh juices are equally impressive — especially the pomegranate juice and the orange-mosambi mix, both refreshing and naturally sweet.
What truly makes the experience special is the warm and polite staff. The service is quick, attentive, and always delivered with a smile. The beautiful interiors create a clean, cozy, and welcoming atmosphere, making you want to sit back and enjoy your meal.

featured_reviews.name: Taran Arora
featured_reviews.review_text: If you enjoy South Indian food and want a cleaner, more café-style experience in Dadar, Mutuswami is worth trying. Best dishes to order are Benne dosa, thatte idli, rasam rice , filter coffee and pineapple sheera.  Staff is very courteous and welcoming.

They have indoor and outdoor seating. Post 8 pm it's a busy schedule for the restaurant so go a bit early to get the best available table of the house.

Our food recommendations.

Overall, it was an okay experience. Some dishes were delightful, but the slow service and a few underwhelming items left room for improvement.

For drinks, I tried the Virgin Mojito and Oreo Milkshake, and both were refreshing and delicious. As starters, we ordered the Rasoi Paneer Tikka and Bhatti Da Murg, which were flavorful, perfectly cooked, and truly satisfying.

For the main course, we had Paneer Nimbu Da Pyaaza with Rumali Roti and Schezwan Fried Rice. Both dishes were excellent, packed with flavor, and complemented each other really well.

To finish the meal, we indulged in their Rasmalai, which was the perfect ending—soft, rich, and absolutely delightful.

Overall, everything from the food to the ambience exceeded expectations. A highly recommended place for anyone looking to enjoy great food and a pleasant dining experience!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Rasoi near Dadar Station and had a wonderful dining experience. The restaurant offers a great mix of North Indian, Malwani, and Chinese cuisine, making it a good option for groups with different food preferences.

We started with the Chicken Sheekh Kebab and Chicken Tikka, both of which were flavorful, juicy, and perfectly cooked. For the main course, we tried the Thai Curry, which was rich, creamy, and packed with authentic flavors.

To accompany our meal, we ordered a Fruit Punch mocktail that was refreshing and well-balanced. We ended the meal with their Sizzling Brownie, which was served hot and was the perfect sweet treat to finish on.

The food quality, taste, and portion sizes were impressive. The service was prompt, and the location near Dadar Station makes it a convenient spot for a satisfying meal. Definitely worth a visit if you're in the area and looking for delicious food across multiple cuisines.

featured_reviews.name: Shraddha Viswakarma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Rasoi recently and honestly, it’s one of those places that just gets everything right. The ambience and decor are super aesthetic yet warm, making it perfect for literally anyone—families, couples or even chill friend scenes.

The place was quite packed when we went, but the crowd added to the vibe instead of feeling chaotic. Service was genuinely top-notch—staff was quick, polite and very attentive.

We tried the Watermelon & Basil Martini and Anar Ka Pyaar—both refreshing and beautifully presented. Starters like Balinese BBQ Chicken and Sigri Murgh were full of flavour and perfectly cooked. For mains, the Nawabi Murgh with Butter Garlic Naan was rich and comforting, and the Chicken Dum Biryani was aromatic and satisfying.

They also had a live singer which elevated the whole experience. Ending it with Mango Kulfi Falooda (seasonal aamras specials!) was just perfect. Great food, great vibe, and totally worth it.

featured_reviews.name: Aafreen Mulla

The live music adds a lovely vibe to the dining experience, and the service was excellent throughout our visit. The staff was polite, attentive, and made us feel comfortable.
The food was absolutely delicious — everything was well-cooked, flavorful, and served fresh. Every dish tasted amazing and was prepared with great quality.
Highly recommended for anyone looking for good food, good music, and a memorable time with family or friends. Must visit this place!

featured_reviews.name: Pranali Kadam

featured_reviews.review_text:
A school friend sent me a reel about Poe and Pao in Chembur. I decided to go chasing Poe and Pao. Since I was already in Bandra, I thought I’d try their Matunga outlet instead.

Now, if you’re a true-blue Mumbaikar, you know traffic jams aren’t an inconvenience, they’re a lifestyle. So there I was, stuck in the middle of one, wishing for a restroom more than anything else.

When I finally reached, they said, “Go next door.” I stumbled into Dakshin Culture Curry and found the cleanest restroom in Mumbai. Small, but spotless. You can’t do pranayama there, but you’ll definitely come out feeling zen.

Feeling human again, I stepped out… and somehow found myself in Diva Maharashtracha. For a moment, I thought I’d taken a wrong turn in life. That’s when someone explained that Dakshin Culture Curry, Goa Portuguesa, and Diva Maharashtracha are a trilogy, same team, shared menu, different cuisines. And Poe and Pao? The latest addition to the family.

One look at the menu, and I knew there was no way I was walking back to Poe and Pao.

I started with a Sushegad Shot (feni, lime, and kaffir leaves) -  Goa in a glass. Then came the Khekade Kalimiri Soup, a crab-and-black-pepper combo that doubles as a natural sinus reliever. After that, Ravas Moile, Tender Coconut Cashew Nut Sukke (their signature dish), Chicken Modak, and Appam n Amboli.

The Chicken Modak was the surprise star—moist chicken kheema wrapped in a soft, pillowy coating. Though, between us, it did look slightly jaundiced.

They ended the meal with complimentary Caramel Custard—light, soft, and just the right sweetness.

The staff were courteous and attentive, the ambience warm and welcoming.

Ambience: A+
Food: A+++

What started as a quest for Poe and Pao turned into a delicious detour, a reminder that some of the best finds in Mumbai happen purely by serendipity.

featured_reviews.name: vru
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Udupi Shri Krishna Restaurant, which is conveniently located just a 1-minute walk from Matunga East Railway Station—making it extremely easy to reach without any hassle.

I learned that the restaurant was inaugurated by Sane Guruji, which adds a nice historical and cultural touch to the place.

When we arrived, we had to wait in the coupon queue, but it was quite smooth. Within about 10 minutes, our name was called. Considering it was a Saturday, the waiting time was very reasonable. I’ve heard that sometimes the wait can go up to 45 minutes to an hour, but we were lucky.

The staff at the counter was very polite and attentive. One thing that stood out was how they reminded everyone to wash their hands before eating—such a small yet thoughtful and caring gesture.

The food is served on a banana leaf, which adds a traditional and authentic feel. The entire meal felt fresh, simple, and very much like home-cooked food.

The thali included:

2 sabjis
1 koshimbir (cucumber salad)
Roti and puri
Curd
Pickle
Buttermilk
Nimbu rasam and regular rasam
Rice with ghee
One sweet (options like rasgulla, halwa, shrikhand, or gulab jamun)

Curd and sweets are limited, while the rest is unlimited.

The taste was excellent—especially the curd and nimbu rasam, which were absolutely delicious. The rasgulla we had was fresh, mildly sweet, and exceeded expectations.

The management and service were top-notch. The staff ensured that hot food was served in every round, which made the experience even better. Overall, it truly felt like having a comforting meal at home.

The full thali costs ₹300, and the mini thali is ₹200, which is quite reasonable for the quality and quantity offered.

My only suggestion would be to introduce a premium thali option at a slightly higher price, including a few more South Indian dishes for those who want to explore more variety.

Overall, a wonderful experience—highly recommended to everyone! 👍

featured_reviews.name: DV
featured_reviews.review_text: This is an iconic eatery that is as old as 84 years. It's is a true treasure for Mumbaikars who like South Indian vegetarian food. It serves a full unlimited meal from the south Indian cuisines with Tamil dishes being prominently cooked and served. It's traditionally served on a banana leaf making it visually appealing. The Thali as it is known has Rasam, Sambar, Dal, Rice with option of ghee atop, Poori, Chapati, 2 dry cooked vegetables and 2 gravy based vegetables. There is curd and flavoured (ginger/coriander) butter milk. There is a choice of dessert; my favourite is the Moong Dal payasam. At a modest 300/- bucks it's absolutely value for money. It's a living testament of cultural bonding between the South Indian community and the local Maharashtrians as well as Gujratis. The fact that it was inaugurated by Sane Guruji makes it even richer in identity.

One of the best places for pure vegetarian food. This place is easily accessible as it is located right on the main road near Sena Bhavan. You can get down at Dadar Metro Station, and as soon as you come onto the main road, the restaurant is right beside it.

Whenever you visit, you will almost always find a rush here. The waiting time can range from 30 minutes to even 1 hour. However, they have now expanded their seating capacity, and there is also a lift available to reach the first floor.

The place is also very reasonably priced. We were a group of four friends and ordered around 7–8 items, yet the total bill was only around ₹1200.

You will find a wide variety of Maharashtrian dishes here, and they have also started serving some South Indian snacks.

Must try: Modak, Aamras, and Misal Pav
You can also try the Batata Vada.

Overall, it is a great place for pure vegetarian food and definitely worth visiting with friends and family.

featured_reviews.name: Mayur Aundhakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Aaswad Uphar Gruh & Mithai recently and had a proper Maharashtrian भोजन experience.
We tried a variety of items including Puri Bhaji, Seasonal Thali, Puran Poli, Lime Juice, Buttermilk, Kothimbir Vadi, and other traditional dishes. The food overall had that authentic, homely Maharashtrian taste which Aaswad is known for.
👉 Taste:
Most dishes were flavorful and well-prepared. The Puran Poli stood out – soft, perfectly sweet, and very satisfying. The Kothimbir Vadi was crispy and nicely spiced. The Seasonal Thali gave a good variety and felt wholesome.
👉 Quantity & Quality:
Portion sizes are decent, and ingredients taste fresh. It gives a proper “ghar jaisa khaana” vibe.
👉 Service & Waiting Time:
Had to wait around 40 minutes, which is quite long. The place gets very crowded, especially during peak hours.
👉 Ambience:
Simple, traditional setup. Nothing fancy, but clean and functional. Seating can feel a bit cramped during rush hours.

featured_reviews.name: Sarika Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Prepared for a long wait, we were pleasantly surprised to find a table for two upon arrival. Being a week day may have also impacted numbers & wait times which otherwise apparently is a lot.
After a thorough scrutiny of the menu, we ordered pithla bhakri and a chaitra thali.
Pithla bhakri plate comes with two types of bhakris, rice & jowari.
The chaitra thali actually is good for two people which we realised when it arrived. Special mention of the jackfruit bhaaji, kajuchi usal and fresh unadulterated aamras with its natural sweetness & taste. The panah was too thick & sweet for my taste. Missed taking a pic of the thali.
My friend ordered puranpoli ice-cream for dessert & relished it. Again that is a huge portion with three scoops, too much for one person. See the pic :)
Definitely worth a visit to savour Maharashtrian cuisine in an iconic old eatery.
P.S. Five minutes walk from Dadar Aqualine metro station.

featured_reviews.name: Sumit K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Aswad Restaurant is an excellent place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food in a clean, comfortable, and welcoming environment in dadar mumbai. The restaurant maintains very high standards of hygiene, which adds greatly to the overall dining experience.

The food is not only delicious but also very affordable, making it a great option for regular meals as well as for first-time visitors wanting to explore traditional Maharashtrian cuisine. Their **Maharashtrian thali** is highly recommended, offering a wholesome and satisfying combination of flavors. Special dishes like **Bhakri–Pithla** and **Thalipeeth** are prepared perfectly and taste truly homely.

One of the highlights of Aswad is their **Modak**, which is simply the best—fresh, flavorful, and a must-try for dessert lovers. The food is mild, not overly spicy or oily, making it suitable for all age groups and ideal for those who prefer healthy, home-style meals.

The service is polite, prompt, and courteous, adding to the pleasant atmosphere of the restaurant. Its convenient location near **Dadar Metro Station** makes it easily accessible in mumbai.

Overall, Aswad Restaurant is a wonderful choice for hygienic, affordable, and authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food with a comforting, home-cooked feel. Highly recommended.
